institution: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, New Delhi
citation: Department of Clinical Microbiology and Immunology, Sir Ganga Ram Hospital. Clinical Microbiology Newsletter, Vol. 26, No. 1: percentage sensitivity, January to December 2019. New Delhi: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital; published June 2020.
reporting: Percent susceptible by specimen (blood, urine, pus/tissue, body fluids, respiratory specimens), organism (Gram-positive and Gram-negative tables) and location (OPD, ward, ICU), with the number of isolates per row; organism counts per specimen and location in bar charts with printed data labels and an "others" list.
method: MIC testing on Vitek 2, interpreted with CLSI 2019 guidelines; repeat isolates excluded (printed in parentheses).

verification.note: All 10 susceptibility tables (GPC and GNB, pages 2 to 6) were parsed from the PDF text layer (pdfplumber word positions; column headers rebuilt from the rotated header text; OPD, ward and ICU taken from each row's background colour and checked against the row order), then every cell and every row n was compared by eye with the pages rendered at scale 4 and cropped into left and right halves: no differences. The body fluid GPC table prints Staphylococci spp. ICU as n = 0 with blank cells; the parser dropped that row and it was restored from the image so that the rows pair with their organisms. Organism charts: bar data labels were matched to the legend swatches by colour and legend order and the "others" lists parsed from the text layer; every panel (bars, legend and others list) was then compared by eye with the chart rendered at scale 4 and checked arithmetically (named bars plus Others equal the printed isolates; the others list sums to Others), and every table n was compared with the chart count of the same organism, specimen and location: all 15 panels balance and all agree. Read from the image because the parse failed: the three body fluid panels (bars not found: OPD K. pneumoniae 12 and Others 49; ward E. coli 13, K. pneumoniae 11, Enterococci spp. 10 and Others 29; ICU Others 48), others-list names split over two lines (blood ICU Enterobacter spp. 7, Ralstonia mannitolilytica 2, Haemophilus influenzae 1, Pseudomonas stutzeri 1; urine ward Burkholderia cepacia 3; pus OPD Stenotrophomonas maltophilia 4) and two pairs of respiratory ward entries run together (Achromobacter spp. 1 and Burkholderia cepacia 1; Serratia spp. 1 and Streptococcus pyogenes Group A 1). The three cells the build does not keep were re-read on the page and are printed as recorded.

notes: Clinical Microbiology Newsletter of Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, Vol. 26, No. 1 (published June 2020), data January to December 2019, 8 pages. The PDF has no direct link: sgrh.com serves it only by an HTTP POST from the Microbiology Newsletter selector on https://sgrh.com/en/publications (issue "June-2020"; the file downloads as mb-june2020.pdf). Pages 2 to 6 give one specimen each (blood; urine; pus/tissue; body fluids; respiratory specimens): organism bar charts for OPD, ward and ICU (samples, positives, isolates with the repeat isolates excluded in parentheses, a data label on every bar and an "others" list) and Gram-positive (GPC) and Gram-negative (GNB) percentage sensitivity tables with three rows per organism (OPD, ward, ICU, by the colour key) and the number of isolates; "-" means not done. Specimens recorded as blood, urine, pus (printed "Pus / Tissue", pus and tissue reported together), sterile (printed "Body fluids") and respiratory. Rows printed "Staphylococci spp." are separate from Staph. aureus and are recorded as coagulase-negative staphylococci, as the 2011 edition labels the same row "Staphylococci spp. (CONS)". Enterococci are reported at genus level only (printed "Enterococci spp.", urine "Enterococcus spp.") and recorded as Enterococcus spp. Combined columns: "Cefoxitin/Oxacillin" is recorded under oxacillin, "Imipenem / Meropenem" (urine, pus and body fluid GNB tables) under meropenem and "Glycopeptides" under vancomycin (vancomycin and teicoplanin reported as one figure), each cell noted; the blood and respiratory GNB tables print "Imipenem" alone (recorded under imipenem) and the body fluid GPC table heads its methicillin column "Cefoxitin" (recorded under cefoxitin). The "Quinolones" column (no agent named) is not recorded. Colistin is printed as percent susceptible in every GNB table and is recorded as printed; urine Proteus prints colistin 0 in OPD and ward. Footnotes: blood S. pneumoniae OPD penicillin is printed "83*" with "*1 isolate IS, 1 isolate R", and respiratory S. pneumoniae OPD ceftriaxone "94*" with "*1 isolate IS"; both are in the cell notes. The body fluid GPC table prints Staphylococci spp. ICU as n = 0 with blank cells. Source inconsistency recorded as printed: body fluid OPD Staphylococci spp. (n = 9) prints penicillin 33 while its Cefoxitin column prints 0 (the build suppresses the penicillin figure). Isolate numbers: every table n equals the chart count of the same organism, specimen and location, and every chart panel balances (named bars plus Others equal the printed isolates; the "others" list sums to Others). Per-drug tested numbers are not printed: 54 of the 820 recorded percentages are not k/n of the row's n (14 of them fit truncation, e.g. blood ICU A. baumannii n = 59, amikacin 13 where 8/59 is 13.6); all but three can be given by a smaller number of tested isolates, and all are recorded as printed. Three can be given by no whole number of tested isolates up to the row's n, rounded or truncated (pus ICU Proteus ertapenem 79 with n = 12; body fluid ward Enterococci spp. high-dose gentamicin 9 and linezolid 76 with n = 10): each is within one point of an achievable figure (the tolerance the app applies to every source for rounding), so it is shown without a caution and the arithmetic is in its cell note. Organism counts: every bar and "others" entry whose organism has a canonical key is recorded, with misspellings mapped to the intended organism ("Klebseilla", "Serratia marscecens", "S. maltophila", "L.monocytogenes", "Elizebethkingia meningoseptica"); "Salmonella entertidis" and "Salmonella typhimurium" are recorded as non-typhoidal Salmonella and "Burkholderia vietnamiensis" as Burkholderia spp.; blood ICU counts Stenotrophomonas maltophilia twice (bar 18 and "S. maltophila-1" in the others list), both recorded. Fungi are counted in the charts as "Fungal isolates" (not recordable); the species also named in the same panels' others lists (blood ICU Cryptococcus neoformans 2, body fluid OPD and ward Candida tropicalis 1 each) are a partial count and are listed in excluded; fungal susceptibility data were deferred to the next issue. Entries without a key, or that would add to the key of a tabulated organism, are listed in excluded. Page 1 (case report: histoplasmosis), page 7 (prescription auditing of antimicrobials and the drug resistance index) and page 8 (case report continued, publications, highlights) carry no susceptibility tables.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 820 cells (the seeded 25% sample of 205 from sample_cells.py, spread over all 10 GPC and GNB tables on pages 2 to 6, plus every other cell), all 94 row n values, the 17 printed table rows not recorded and all 272 organism counts were read from the page images (tables at scale 3 cut into halves with the row labels and n kept; the 15 chart panels at scale 4) and checked against an independent word-position parse of the text layer that takes OPD, ward and ICU from each cell's own fill colour: image and parse agree on all 111 printed table rows.

Result: 0 transcription errors; no value, n or count changed. OPD, ward and ICU correct on every row (yellow, blue and pink fills, in that order in every triple of every table); the organism label of every row triple and the specimen of every page correct; every printed value of a recorded column is in the file and nothing else is; the 17 rows not recorded are exactly the rows printed all "-" or blank, as excluded says. No table reached the 2% error threshold.

Columns: all 14 Cefoxitin/Oxacillin cells (under oxacillin), all 33 Imipenem / Meropenem cells (urine, pus and body fluid GNB, under meropenem) and all 31 Glycopeptides cells (under vancomycin) carry their cell note; the blood and respiratory GNB tables print Imipenem alone (under imipenem) and the body fluid GPC table heads its methicillin column Cefoxitin alone (under cefoxitin); Quinolones not recorded. Every header of every table was checked against the rotated header text and the image.

Specific items confirmed on the page: body fluid GPC Staphylococci spp. ICU prints n = 0 with blank cells (no row); blood S. pneumoniae OPD penicillin "83*" with "*1 isolate IS, 1 isolate R" and respiratory S. pneumoniae OPD ceftriaxone "94*" with "*1 isolate IS", both recorded as 83 and 94 with the footnote in the cell note.

Charts: every panel balances on the image (named bars plus Others equal the printed isolates; the others list sums to Others; body fluid bars, pus ICU "Streptococcus agalactiae1" and body fluid ICU "Pseudomonas aeruginosa5" read from the image); bar order equals legend order in every panel (blood ICU A. baumannii 59 and Acinetobacter spp. 11 share a colour); all 111 table n equal their chart count; the 272 counts are exactly the recordable bar and others entries, the rest named in excluded.

Cells the build does not keep, re-read: urine Proteus OPD and ward colistin 0, and body fluid OPD Staphylococci spp. penicillin 33 beside Cefoxitin 0, are printed that way (source, not transcription).

Added by the second reader (values unchanged): conflict entries and cell notes for the three percentages that no whole number of tested isolates up to the row's n gives, rounded or truncated (pus ICU Proteus ertapenem 79, n = 12; body fluid ward Enterococci spp. high-dose gentamicin 9 and linezolid 76, n = 10), matching how the 2021 edition treats its two such cells; the notes sentence that said every such percentage could be given by a smaller number of tested isolates was corrected.

Lead 2026-09-26: the conflict entries the second reader added for three cells within one point of an achievable figure (pus ICU Proteus ertapenem 79; body fluid ward Enterococci high-dose gentamicin 9 and linezolid 76) were removed for consistency with every other source (the build tolerates one point of rounding); the arithmetic stays in the cell notes.

Lead 2026-09-26: fungal chart entries follow one rule across the SGRH editions: recorded as counts unless the same panel also prints an unnamed fungal entry (then a partial count, excluded): moved to excluded: blood icu Cryptococcus neoformans 2; sterile opd Candida tropicalis 1; sterile ward Candida tropicalis 1.

excluded.what: Quinolones column of every GPC and GNB table (pages 2 to 6)
excluded.why: drug class with no agent named, no canonical drug key (blood Salmonella typhi prints 2 (OPD) and 2 (ward), Salmonella paratyphi A 3 and 0)

excluded.what: Rows printed with every drug not done ("-") or with no isolates
excluded.why: no values: blood Salmonella typhi ICU (n=3), Salmonella paratyphi A ICU (n=1), A. baumannii OPD (n=2) and ward (n=7); urine Staphylococci spp. ward (n=6) and ICU (n=0), Staph. aureus ICU (n=2), Proteus ICU (n=9); pus Staphylococci spp. ward (n=8) and ICU (n=0), Enterobacter ICU (n=7); body fluids Staphylococci spp. ward (n=1) and ICU (n=0, blank cells), Enterococci spp. OPD (n=3) and ICU (n=7), K. pneumoniae ICU (n=6); respiratory Staph. aureus OPD (n=5)

excluded.what: Page 7: prescription auditing of antimicrobials (DDD per 100 bed days, 2019, total 149.60) and the drug resistance index 2009 to 2019 (2019: E. coli 0.58, K. pneumoniae 0.78, A. baumannii 0.56, P. aeruginosa 0.40)
excluded.why: antimicrobial consumption and a composite resistance index, not percent susceptible

excluded.what: Page 8: highlights based on blood isolates IPD (ACCo in S. Typhi 3.04%; overall prevalence of MRSA, VRE, ESBL and CRE 0.08%, 0.06%, 0.67% and 0.43%; MRSA isolation rate 62.9% of S. aureus; VRE 32.8% of 74 enterococci; ESBL 89.4% and CRE 70.4% of 266 Enterobacteriaceae)
excluded.why: phenotype summaries, not drug-level percent susceptible; they do not all agree with the blood rows (the 74 enterococci are the ward and ICU rows, 21 + 53, which print glycopeptides 52 and 62)

excluded.what: Organism count entries with no canonical organism key
excluded.why: not recordable: Fungal isolates, Histoplasma capsulatum, Rhodotorula spp., Achromobacter spp., Alcaligenes faecalis, Bacillus spp. (also "Bacillus sp."), Brevundimonas (printed "Brevudimonas spp."), Chryseobacterium (printed "Chrysobacterium spp."), Corynebacterium spp., Diphtheroids, Haemophilus spp. (printed "Haemophilus sps."), Leclercia adecarboxylata, Moraxella spp., Myroides (printed "Myroides sps."), Nocardia spp., Ochrobactrum anthropi, Pantoea agglomerans, Pantoea (printed "Pantoea sps."), Pseudomonas putida, Pseudomonas stutzeri, Ralstonia mannitolilytica, Ralstonia pickettii, "Vibrio species"

excluded.what: Organism count entries that would add to the key of a tabulated organism
excluded.why: Acinetobacter spp. (key of the A. baumannii rows), Klebsiella spp. (printed "Klebseilla spp.", key of the K. pneumoniae rows), Pseudomonas spp. (printed "Pseudomonas sps.", resolves to P. aeruginosa), Salmonella spp. (typhoidal Salmonella group, the parent of the S. Typhi and S. Paratyphi A rows): recording them would misstate the tabulated organism's isolate count
